stem:
Sonia ties thread on a circular board with $10$ pegs, stepping a fixed gap of $4$ pegs each time. She asks whether the thread will eventually reach every peg.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Answer with the phrase thread-gap alone, instead of checking whether $10$ and $4$ share a common factor.
Say that reaching every peg is what creates the co-primality of $10$ and $4$.
No: $10$ and $4$ share common factor $2$, so stepping by $4$ repeats a smaller cycle and misses some pegs.
Treat the question as only asking whether $10$ and $4$ are co-prime, without linking that fact to the cyclic peg walk.

teacher.key_rationale: gcd(10,4)=2>1, so the walk cycles on a proper subset and misses pegs. Naming thread-gap alone swaps the decision for a label. Saying reach creates co-primality reverses the prediction. Checking co-primality with no link to the peg walk conflates a different task.
